result.topic_en: Euler generalizes his series-to-continued-fraction theorem to alternating series with arbitrary numerators (Theorem III), then illustrates it with the series 1−1+1−… = 1/2 and with the series 1/2 − 2/3 + 3/4 − … = l2 − 1/2.

§. 27. Tribuamus nunc etiam seriei initio assumtae
$\frac{1}{\alpha}-\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{1}{\gamma}-\frac{1}{\delta}+$ etc.
numeratores quoscunque, sitque
$s=\frac{a}{\alpha}-\frac{b}{\beta}+\frac{c}{\gamma}-\frac{d}{\delta}+$ etc.
atque in Theoremate primo loco litterarum $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. scribi oportet $\frac{\alpha}{a}, \frac{\beta}{b}, \frac{\gamma}{c}, \frac{\delta}{d}$, etc. quo facto fractio continua ita se habebit:
$\frac{1}{s}=\frac{\alpha}{a}+\cfrac{\frac{\alpha\alpha}{aa}}{\frac{\beta}{b}-\frac{\alpha}{a}+\cfrac{\frac{\beta\beta}{bb}}{\frac{\gamma}{c}-\frac{\beta}{b}+\cfrac{\frac{\gamma\gamma}{cc}}{\frac{\delta}{d}-\frac{\gamma}{c}+\text{etc.}}}}$
Iam ad fractiones tollendas prima fractio supra et infra multiplicetur per $ab$, secunda per $bc$, tertia per $cd$, et ita porro; tum vero utrinque per $a$ multiplicando obtinebitur
$\frac{a}{s}=\alpha+\cfrac{\alpha\alpha b}{a\beta-b\alpha+\cfrac{\alpha c\beta\beta}{b\gamma-c\beta+\cfrac{bd\gamma\gamma}{c\delta-d\gamma+\text{etc.}}}}$
Hinc igitur formetur sequens
Theorema III.
§. 28. Si proposita fuerit series infinita huius formae
$s=\frac{a}{\alpha}-\frac{b}{\beta}+\frac{c}{\gamma}-\frac{d}{\delta}+$ etc.
ex ea formabitur sequens fractio continua:

§. 29. Ad hoc illustrandum proposita sit haec series:
$\frac{1}{1}-\frac{2}{2}+\frac{3}{3}-\frac{4}{4}+\frac{5}{5}-$ etc. $=\frac{1}{2}$,
ita ut sit $s=\frac{1}{2}$; fractio ergo continua hinc orta erit
$2=1+\cfrac{2}{0+\cfrac{3.4}{0+\cfrac{8.9}{0+\cfrac{15.16}{0+\text{etc.}}}}}$
quae forma reducitur ad istud productum infinitum:
$2=1+\frac{2.1^2.4.2^2.6.3^2.8.4^2.\text{etc.}}{1.3.2^2.5.3^2.7.4^2.9.\text{etc.}}$ [?]

items.english: Theorem III: if an infinite series of the form s = a/α − b/β + c/γ − d/δ + etc. is given, the following continued fraction is formed from it: a/s = α + ααb/(aβ − bα + αcββ/(bγ − cβ + …)).

items.quote: Nullum vero dubium esse potest, quin valor istius producti sit $=1$.
items.english: But there can be no doubt that the value of this product is = 1.
